title: an error reading the decision records in the board's background timers never kills the board: the merge-recovery timer skips the tick and retries, and every timer callback that can throw is guarded
acceptance: Why. On 2026-10-05 an unsharded audit of main in ubuntu:24.04 linux/arm64 (bun 1.4.2) failed tests/board-live-stream.test.sh deterministically (3 of 3) with 'file replacement disconnected the SSE stream'. Instrumented, the board process logged `ENOENT ... scandir state/decisions` at `readResponses` (board/server.ts:640-644) <- `anyRunning` (:1846) <- the bare `setInterval(() => { if (anyRunning()) void recover(); }, 1000)` (:1848), and then exited. The one-shot fault the suite injects (tests/lib/board-read-race.ts) is consumed by whichever timer reads state/decisions first: the SSE poll timer (:2131-2139) wraps its read in try/catch and survives; the one-second merge-recovery timer has no guard, so the exception is uncaught and ends the whole Bun process. x64 and macOS pass only because the SSE timer happens to read first there. This is a real latent board bug: any readdir/stat/JSON error in that timer (an ENOENT while a decisions directory is replaced, EMFILE, EIO, EACCES, a registry read failing inside `stores()` :602) kills the captain's board, dropping every SSE connection and the tracking of running merges. The same unguarded call runs once at module load (:1847), where a throw stops the board from starting.

Guard the merge-recovery timer and its startup call (board/server.ts only). (a) The startup call at :1847 and the interval body at :1848 run inside try/catch: an exception skips this tick and the next tick (one second later) tries again; the interval itself is never cleared by an error. (b) `recover` (:1821-1845) also reads `readResponses()` in its `for` header, outside its per-record try, and its outer block is a try/finally with no catch, so a throw there still rejects the promise. Add a `catch` to that outer try (keeping the `finally` that clears `recovering`): it logs through the (c) path and does not rethrow, so the promise resolves and `void recover()` never produces an unhandled rejection. The per-record try/catch inside the loop is unchanged. (c) Logging: each distinct error message is written once to stderr as `fm-board: merge recovery skipped a tick: <message>` (a module-level Set of messages already logged), so a persistent failure does not flood the log; no event is emitted and nothing is written under state/. (d) Behaviour on success is byte-for-byte today's: the same calls, in the same order, at the same interval; a running merge is still settled on the first successful tick after the error clears.

Audit the other timer and child callbacks in board/server.ts and state the result in the PR body. On current main they are: `setTimeout(() => child.kill(), 60_000)` (:1756) and `setTimeout(() => p.kill(), 20_000)` (:1807) and `setTimeout(() => child.kill('SIGTERM'), reloginTimeout)` (:1993) - kill on an exited child does not throw in Bun, leave them; `setTimeout(() => settled('running'), 3000)` (:1782) - cannot throw, leave it; the SSE poll timer (:2131) - already guarded, leave it; the SSE heartbeat `setInterval(() => c.enqueue(...), 15000)` (:2140) and the `watch(PUBLIC, () => send('reload', {}))` callback (:2145) - `enqueue` on a controller that has been closed or errored throws, so wrap each body in try/catch that, on error, clears both intervals and closes the watcher (the same `stop` the cancel path runs), never rethrowing. The merge helper's `child.on('error')` and `child.on('exit')` handlers (:1686-1690) call `settle`, which has its own try/catch (:1620-1623), and `reasonOf` guards its read, so they cannot throw: leave them and list them. Any additional unguarded timer/child callback that can throw, found on the branch's base, is guarded the same way and listed; none is changed in behaviour on success.

Fault injection, one change, tests/lib/board-read-race.ts only: the race marker may carry an optional integer `skip` (default 0): the first `skip` matching calls (same operation and path) pass through untouched and decrement `skip` in the marker file; the next matching call is faulted exactly as today (marker removed, path renamed away for that one call, restored in finally). Without `skip` the facade behaves byte-for-byte as today, so every existing case in tests/board-live-stream.test.sh is unchanged.

Tests in tests/board-live-stream.test.sh (134 lines now), in the existing Python block, placed before the 'Keep a stream open' loop and after the initial-stream case, with no SSE stream open and no HTTP request in flight while a fault is armed, so only the one-second timer can consume it on every platform: (1) arm `{'operation':'readdirSync','path':<root>/state/decisions}`; wait (poll the marker every 100 ms, at most 5 s, making no HTTP request) until the marker is gone; then sleep 1.5 s and assert `state()` answers 200 twice, one second apart; assertion message 'the merge-recovery timer survives a failed read of state/decisions'. Red on base on every platform (the uncaught throw ends the process, so `state()` cannot connect). (2) write `state/decisions/D-9.json` = `{'id':'D-9','kind':'merge','merge':'running','pr':9}` so `anyRunning()` is true and `recover()` runs every tick; arm the same fault with `skip: 1` so `anyRunning`'s read passes and `recover`'s own `readResponses()` read is the one that fails; wait as in (1); assert `state()` is 200 twice and `state/decisions/D-9.json` still has `merge: 'running'` after the tick (with no registry `repoOf` is null, so `githubState` answers null and recovery only marks it unknown; it never settles it), message 'merge recovery survives a failed read and keeps the running record'. Red on base (unhandled rejection or uncaught throw). Then remove D-9.json before the following cases so the rest of the suite runs exactly as today. (3) a guard for the heartbeat/watch path is not required to be red on base (it needs a closed controller, which the suite cannot force deterministically); the audit in the PR body covers it.

Callers and fixtures checked: tests/lib/board-read-race.ts is imported only by tests/board-live-stream.test.sh (grep `board-read-race` in tests/ and bin/); no other suite injects faults into board/server.ts. `readResponses`, `anyRunning` and `recover` are used only inside board/server.ts. Suites that start the real board and must stay green unchanged (they never arm a fault and see no behaviour change on success): tests/board.test.sh, board-auth, board-card-effects, board-identity, board-pr-links, board-progress, board-projects, board-readiness, board-state, board-task-actions, board-task-grammar, board-titles, board-wake, decisions, crew-end-to-end, diagram, gate, i18n, open, ready, session and watch (.test.sh), the Playwright specs under tests/e2e/ (started through tests/e2e/lib/fixture.ts -> tests/lib/e2e_board_process.py), and tests/merge.test.sh, whose tests/lib/merge_board_binding.py (run at tests/merge.test.sh:440) starts the real board with stderr merged into the stdout pipe it reads for the port line and drives `running` merge records to settlement: that is the path this task guards, and on success it sees byte-identical behaviour and no new output (the new stderr line is written only when a read fails). tests/concurrent-projects.test.sh, through tests/lib/concurrent_projects.py:92-93, extracts `const mergeOf = ...` from board/server.ts by regex and runs it: `mergeOf`'s text is left untouched by this task, so that extraction is unchanged. The log line is new stderr text only; no test asserts the board's stderr is empty (checked: none of those suites asserts the board's log is empty).

Design, edited in place in its home section (T-189 rule; nothing appended at the end of design.md): design/design.md §5.2 'Captain decisions', the paragraph '**A `running` merge whose outcome was never written is recovered by the board.**' (about :463-486). Add one sentence after the bullet list that keeps the paragraph's 'writer-pushed, never a PID/directory polling loop' and 'no local liveness polling' clauses true: the board's own existing re-read of its decision records, which only looks for a record still saying `running`, never stops the board when it fails: a failed read skips that tick (logged once per distinct error) and is retried on the next, and this is a read of the board's own records, not liveness polling of a helper or its directories, so completion and ownership stay writer-pushed as stated above. No other sentence of the paragraph changes.

In flight. PR #198 (T-209, the board drains and replaces itself) also edits board/server.ts (new /drain route and write-route guards), not the timer lines this task touches; whichever of #198 and this task merges second updates its branch and keeps both changes. The running captain board on 127.0.0.1:4173 keeps today's code until it is restarted (after T-209 lands it replaces itself when idle); nothing is migrated: no stored record, event or state file changes shape.

Workers do not run the suites. Evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates. Fail-first is expected from tests/board-live-stream.test.sh cases (1) and (2), red on base on every platform because only the unguarded one-second timer reads state/decisions while the fault is armed; every existing case in that suite is a regression guard and stays as it is. No vendor stub is involved.
